title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: What is structurally wrong with deflection as a metric?
options: It is difficult to compute consistently across channels
It counts an abandoned conversation and a confidently wrong answer identically to a genuine fix, because all three look like "didn't come back"
It excludes contacts that arrive outside business hours
It cannot be benchmarked against other organizations
questions.explanation: Which is why the module replaces it with repeat contact, escalation appropriateness, answer correctness against the governing document, and voluntary return.

questions.prompt: Which of IBM's AskHR figures does the module say is the useful one, and why? `[V]`
options: The 94% containment, because it demonstrates achievable scale
The 75% ticket reduction, because it is the longest-running measure
The residual ~6%, because that is where every hard case lives and it is the module's entire legal surface
The 40% cost reduction, because it is what funds the programme
questions.explanation: A design that handles 94% beautifully and routes the remaining 6% badly has concentrated the problem rather than solved it. Note also that the 94% is unaudited self-report.

questions.prompt: Why does the module say the model is not the variable for this use case?
options: Because all current models perform equivalently on HR questions

Because a capable model reading a superseded document produces a fluent, confident, wrong answer, while a weaker model reading a current one produces a correct answer — the document set determines whether the answer is true
Because model quality cannot be evaluated without benchmarks
Because vendors do not disclose which model they use
questions.explanation: Model quality shows up in tone and edge cases. Document-set quality shows up in whether the answer is true, which is where the spending should go.

questions.prompt: How does the module characterize an answer drawn from a superseded document?
options: A retrieval error to be fixed in configuration
A misstatement made by the employer, in writing, to an employee, about their own money or health
A model hallucination
An acceptable risk if the error rate is low
questions.explanation: The model did not get it wrong; the corpus did, and the model repeated it faithfully. C is the specific misdiagnosis to avoid — nothing was fabricated.

questions.prompt: Which corpus control does the module call the single best one?
options: Removing superseded documents from the index rather than marking them superseded
An effective-date field on every retrievable document, with a rule that the capability may not answer from a document lacking one
A named owner per topic
Quarterly review of the full document set
questions.explanation: Because it converts an invisible failure into a refusal — a capability that says "I can't answer that, here's who can" is enormously better than one that answers from a 2021 wiki page. A is the highest-yield *hour*; B is the best standing control.

questions.prompt: What does "notice to the bot is notice to you" mean in practice? `[V]`
options: That all chatbot conversations must be reviewed by HR staff
That employees must be warned not to disclose medical information to the assistant

That an employee's message may put the employer on notice of an FMLA or ADA obligation whether or not anyone at the company reads it — which makes escalation routing a legal control rather than a design preference
That chatbots must be disabled for leave and accommodation topics
questions.explanation: Counsel frame this exposure in *may* and we found no controlling decision, which is why the module carries a counsel gate. D over-corrects: the answer is routing design, not prohibition.

questions.prompt: Why does keyword-based escalation routing fail?
options: Because employees deliberately avoid trigger words to bypass the system
Because people do not use the words — "I'm struggling to get in for 9am since my treatment started" is an accommodation request containing neither the word accommodation nor disability
Because keyword lists cannot be maintained across languages
Because models cannot reliably detect keywords in long messages
questions.explanation: So route on topic proximity and uncertainty rather than vocabulary, and accept an asymmetric false-positive rate: over-routing costs a coordinator's time, under-routing costs a statutory obligation nobody noticed.

questions.prompt: Why does the module insist on keeping a human route no harder to find than the bot? `[V]`
options: Because employees prefer human contact in most surveys

Because accessibility obligations, and the fact that a capability which is the only route to a deadline makes access the difference between meeting that deadline and missing it — while adoption pressure pushes the other way
Because AI disclosure requirements mandate an alternative channel
Because deflection targets should be capped
questions.explanation: And Module 2's IBM case is the evidence: removing the human route drove satisfaction from +19 to −35. C is not what Article 50 requires — that is about disclosure, not alternatives.
